name: Raven Darkhölme

summary: Almost nothing about Mystique's beginnings is certain, and even the name Raven Darkhölme is one she chose. She has said her powers surfaced when she was twelve and that she had to fight just to stay alive, and her shape-changing body has kept her going far past a normal lifespan; by her own account she is well over a hundred years old. Toward the end of the 19th century she met Irene Adler, an Austrian mutant who had filled thirteen volumes with visions of the late 20th and early 21st centuries and been left blind by the effort. Raven agreed to help decode the books and to stop the worst of them from coming true. The two became lifelong partners and lovers, and by 1895 Raven was even solving London cases as the detective "Sherlock Holmes" with Irene at her side.

The decades that followed were a run of borrowed identities and broken trust. In 1921 she slipped free of a Mexican firing squad alongside a drifter called Logan, recruited him for a Kansas City bank job and then tipped off the police so the rest of her crew took the fall. Posing as a German agent, she had a short affair with Victor Creed, the future Sabretooth, and later walked away from their son Graydon when he turned out to have no powers. Married in human guise to the German nobleman Christian Wagner, she secretly carried on with Irene, who became pregnant, apparently while Raven wore the shape of the mutant Azazel. Raven killed the suspicious baron, passed the pregnancy off as her own and fled when villagers attacked the blue-skinned baby, who grew up to be Nightcrawler. Years later she and Irene took in a gun-toting runaway from Mississippi named Anna Marie and raised her for about a decade as their foster daughter, the future Rogue.

As Raven Darkhölme she climbed the federal civil service to become deputy director of DARPA inside the Defense Department, a post that handed her military secrets and experimental weapons to use for her own ends. That is the role she had when readers first met her in 1978, as a shadowy figure in the pages of Ms. Marvel who soon boards the S.H.I.E.L.D. Helicarrier wearing Nick Fury's face to steal the secret Centurion project. Before long she founded a new Brotherhood of Evil Mutants, borrowing the name of Magneto's old group, with Irene, now called Destiny, alongside Avalanche, the Blob and Pyro, and announced it to the world by trying to assassinate Senator Robert Kelly.

comics.title: The spy inside the Pentagon
comics.summary: Mystique's first appearance is a fleeting cameo in Ms. Marvel #16. A month later she and an accomplice get aboard the S.H.I.E.L.D. Helicarrier, with Raven disguised as Nick Fury, and walk off with the top-secret Centurion project, nearly getting caught by Valentina Allegra de Fontaine on the way out. The stolen hardware is then turned on Ms. Marvel, and while the armoured Centurion fights Carol Danvers and the Avengers across the city, Raven calmly reports back to her superiors.

comics.title: Days of Future Past
comics.summary: Mystique's Brotherhood of Evil Mutants storms the Senate to kill Senator Kelly, whose death in one timeline leads to a future ruled by Sentinels; the adult mind of Kate Pryde is sent back into her teenage body to warn the X-Men. Raven poses as a security guard to gas and grab Professor X and Moira MacTaggert, then fights the X-Men disguised as Nightcrawler until the real one unmasks her; noticing their resemblance, she tells him to ask his foster mother about it. Kate spoils Destiny's crossbow shot at the last moment and Destiny is arrested, while Mystique gets away.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: Uncanny X-Men Vol 1 #142

comics.title: Rogue's flight to the X-Men
comics.summary: Raised and trained by Mystique, Rogue joins the Brotherhood and permanently absorbs Carol Danvers' powers and memories in a fight with her. Haunted by Carol's psyche, Rogue later runs to Professor X for help, and Mystique, convinced her daughter has been brainwashed, sends the Brotherhood after the X-Men. Disguised as Rogue she tries to shoot Xavier, but he turns the shot into a graze; the real Rogue catches her and talks her into letting her stay, and Raven trades Xavier's life for her team's freedom, resenting him from then on.

comics.title: Freedom Force and the death of Destiny
comics.summary: With anti-mutant feeling rising, Mystique offers the Brotherhood's services to the government through Valerie Cooper. After bringing in Magneto, who in fact gives himself up, the team is renamed Freedom Force and Raven receives a presidential pardon that holds only as long as her people stay out of trouble. During a mission to Muir Island against the Reavers she assigns Forge to guard Destiny, but Destiny talks him into leaving and is killed by a mind-controlled Legion. Raven blames Forge and swears he will pay.

comics.title: Dream's End
comics.summary: Shaken by revelations about Destiny and her own role in her son Graydon's death, Mystique reforms the Brotherhood for another try at Senator Kelly, which fails when Pyro switches sides to save him. Impersonating Moira MacTaggert, she twists the Legacy Virus into a weapon aimed at humans, blows up Moira's research centre and leaves her fatally hurt. When Rogue confronts her, Raven stabs her, only for Rogue to recover through borrowed healing and strike back with bone claws. From a hospital bed Mystique tells the X-Men that Destiny's grim forecasts keep coming true no matter what she does.

comics.title: Xavier's deniable agent
comics.summary: After Xavier's previous covert operative is murdered, he breaks Mystique out of a death sentence and offers protection from the many governments hunting her if she works his missions without killing anyone, with Forge on tech and Shortpack as her handler. When the Quiet Man offers her freedom in exchange for Xavier's death, she fakes an attempt on the professor to fool him, which also convinces the X-Men and leads Rogue to disown her. Raven kills the Quiet Man, and after a last kiss with Forge she slips away with the device that hides her from her pursuers.

comics.era: The first mutant birth since M-Day
comics.title: Messiah Complex
comics.summary: Having joined the X-Men under false pretences, Mystique turns on them during a Marauders raid, shooting Rogue and beating Iceman. Her treachery turns out to be a plan to save Rogue, who lies in a coma after absorbing millions of minds. Raven shoves Mister Sinister into Rogue's lethal touch, killing him, and presses the newborn mutant baby to her daughter's face as Destiny's diaries foretold. Rogue wakes cured but carrying her mother's memories, and tries to kill her; Wolverine later tracks Raven to Afghanistan and leaves her alone in the desert.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: New X-Men Vol 2 #46

comics.title: House of X
comics.summary: Mystique signs on to help Xavier and Magneto build the island nation of Krakoa after they promise to resurrect Destiny. She plants a Krakoan flower on the Moon, steals data on Nimrod with Sabretooth and Toad, and dies on the mission to destroy the Orchis Mother Mold when she is blown out into space. The Five bring her back as one of Krakoa's heroes, and she takes a seat on the Quiet Council alongside Exodus and Mister Sinister.

comics.title: Inferno
comics.summary: When Xavier and Magneto keep refusing to resurrect Destiny, Raven recalls a prophecy telling her to bring Irene back and burn down any island of hope that refused. Disguised as Xavier, she has the Five revive Destiny in a younger body, then lines up enough votes to seat her on the Quiet Council. Learning that Moira MacTaggert secretly lives and had been shaping events through repeated lives, Mystique snatches her from Orchis and strips her powers, but Cypher and Krakoa intervene before she can kill her.

comics.title: Back in the shadows
comics.summary: With Krakoa gone, Mystique returns to the world's underground and draws the attention of Nick Fury and S.H.I.E.L.D. in her second solo series. The trail runs through Madripoor, and during the series Fabian Cortez temporarily boosts her powers so that she can copy the abilities of the mutants she imitates, including Magneto's magnetism and Juggernaut's strength. The story builds to a face-to-face confrontation with Fury.

screen.title: X-Men
screen.summary: Working for Magneto, Mystique takes the place of an aide to Senator Kelly so that she and Toad can kidnap him for Magneto's mutation machine. She also borrows the faces of several X-Men to sow confusion. At the Statue of Liberty she duels Wolverine, poses as Storm to get close to him and is run through by his claws, but survives and slips away in the shape of a fallen police officer.

screen.title: X2
screen.summary: With the real Senator Kelly dead, Mystique carries on in his place and impersonates William Stryker's aide to copy files on Magneto's plastic prison. In human form she drugs one of the prison guards and injects him with liquid metal, which Magneto later uses to escape. She joins the uneasy alliance with the X-Men at Alkali Lake, but disguised as Stryker she persuades his son Jason to turn the copied Cerebro against humanity, then leaves with Magneto and Pyro.

screen.title: X-Men: The Last Stand
screen.summary: Captured while hunting for files on the new mutant cure, Mystique refuses to give up Magneto and is held in a prison truck until he frees her. Moments later she steps in front of a cure dart meant for him and loses her powers. Magneto leaves her behind as no longer one of them, and she retaliates by telling the government where he is and what he plans.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: X-Men: The Last Stand

screen.title: X-Men: First Class
screen.actor: Jennifer Lawrence; Morgan Lily as young Raven
screen.summary: As a hungry child, Raven breaks into the Xavier mansion disguised as Charles's mother, and he takes her in as a sister. In 1962 she joins the CIA's new team of young mutants, bonds with Hank McCoy over wanting to look normal, but refuses his serum after Erik Lehnsherr urges her to be proud of her blue form. After the Cuban missile showdown she leaves Charles to join Erik's Brotherhood; Romijn briefly appears as one of her transformations.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: X-Men: First Class (film)

screen.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
screen.summary: In 1973 Raven is hunting Bolivar Trask after finding autopsy files on friends killed in his experiments, and her plan to kill him is the event that leads to a future of Sentinels. Charles, Hank and a time-travelling Logan try to stop her at a Paris peace summit, where Erik shoots her. At the White House she poses as the president, brings down Erik and then, at Charles's urging, spares Trask, and the film closes with her disguised as Stryker taking custody of Logan.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: X-Men: Days of Future Past (film)

screen.title: X-Men: Apocalypse
screen.summary: A decade on, Raven is working alone and pulls the young Nightcrawler out of an East Berlin cage fight before bringing word to Charles that Erik has resurfaced. Captured by Stryker, she escapes with the others and joins the fight in Cairo, where her disguise as Psylocke helps persuade Magneto to turn on Apocalypse. She ends the film training the new X-Men.

screen.title: Dark Phoenix
screen.summary: Set in 1992, the film follows the X-Men after a rescue in space leaves Jean Grey filled with a cosmic force she cannot control. Raven is killed when Jean, under the Phoenix Force's influence, turns on her, a loss that drives Hank to side with Magneto against Jean.

trivia.fact: Mystique's earliest published appearance is now counted as Marvel Preview #5 (April 1976), an adaptation of The Hound of the Baskervilles. Immortal X-Men #8 (2023) revealed that the Sherlock Holmes of Marvel's history was Raven in disguise, making that story her unofficial debut two years before Ms. Marvel #16.

Marvel Fandom wiki: Immortal X-Men Vol 1 #8 (January 2023)

trivia.fact: Chris Claremont has said he originally wanted Mystique and Destiny to be Nightcrawler's biological parents, with Mystique taking male form, but Marvel would not allow it at the time. The idea finally became canon in X-Men Blue: Origins #1, cover-dated January 2024.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: X-Men Blue: Origins Vol 1 #1 (January 2024)

trivia.fact: The wiki counts Deadpool among Mystique's spouses: a flashback in Deadpool #27 (2014), the issue built around Deadpool's wedding, shows her posing as a woman named Lurleen.

Unlike her film counterparts, the comics Mystique was never Magneto's lieutenant. Before Magneto's own X-Men team of the 2010s, the two had crossed paths only a handful of times and barely knew each other.

unverified: First appearance: the Marvel Fandom wiki lists Marvel Preview #5 (April 1976, as Sherlock Holmes) as a retroactive first appearance, Ms. Marvel #16 (April 1978) as her first appearance as Mystique (a cameo) and Ms. Marvel #18 (June 1978) as her first full appearance. This file uses Ms. Marvel #16.

Creators: the character page credits Archie Goodwin, Frank Thorne, Chris Claremont and Jim Mooney. Goodwin and Thorne made Marvel Preview #5, which only became a Mystique story through the 2023 retcon, so the file lists Claremont and Mooney, who made the Ms. Marvel issues.

Avengers: Doomsday (listed as unreleased) is the only film on the MCU Wiki's Mystique page and on Rebecca Romijn's MCU Wiki actor page, so there is no MCU entry. It was left out and no plot details were researched.
Avengers: Endgame Encore re-release (25 September 2026): the MCU Wiki's Encore-exclusive cast list and plot summary do not include Mystique in any version, so no entry was added.
Deadpool & Wolverine (2024) is left out: the MCU Wiki says only archive footage of Romijn from X-Men and X2 was used in its credits sequence.
Animated appearances (including X-Men '97) are excluded under the live-action rule and were not checked in detail.

X-Men: First Class actor field: Romijn's uncredited cameo, as one of Mystique's transformations, is noted on both Fox Mystique pages. It is folded into the Lawrence entry rather than listed separately, and the entry is not flagged as a cameo because Lawrence's role is a lead.

X-Men: Days of Future Past: the film page also lists a flash-only glimpse of the original-timeline Mystique. It is covered by the same entry. Actors who played Mystique's disguises in the Fox films (for example Peter Dinklage and Hugh Jackman) are not listed as Mystique actors.

Dark Phoenix: the Marvel Fandom film page has only a one-paragraph premise. Raven's death and its effect on Hank come from the Raven Darkhölme (Earth-10005) and Henry McCoy (Earth-10005) character pages.

The Earth-616 history on the Marvel Fandom wiki stops after Inferno (2022). The After Krakoa era is built from the page overview, its powers section (which cites Mystique Vol 2 #3-4 for the Cortez boost) and the solicitations on the Mystique Vol 2 issue pages, none of which have plot synopses.

Several issue pages have no synopsis (Uncanny X-Men #388, Mystique #23 and #24, X-Men #203 and #207, New X-Men Vol 2 #46, X-Men Vol 5 #20, X-Men Blue: Origins #1), so those details rest on the character page.
Ms. Marvel #17's synopsis names Mystique's accomplice Geoffrey Ballard, while #18 unmasks Centurion as George Bullard. The era leaves the accomplice unnamed.
Age: the wiki's notes infer from her remarks that she may have been born before 1800. A 1983 story implied she was born around 1953, which the wiki says has been retconned away.
Nightcrawler's conception: the wiki says Irene became pregnant presumably while Raven was in Azazel's form; the origin keeps that hedge.
